note: NY-open read, Mon 2026-11-23 (~7:30 AM CT). Dollar steady near its 19-month high — DXY 103.91 — as the relief bounce faded; Fed Dec hike now ~96% (CME FedWatch via Reuters), the 50bp tail fully priced out. European flash PMIs: Germany carried the bloc (mfg 55.0, a 56-month high; composite 55.0) while France sank deeper (mfg 47.9, a 12-month low; composite 46.2) and the UK missed both (services 52.0, a five-month low). Chicago Fed's October activity index slipped to -0.06 (Sep revised to +0.05) — below-trend growth, and the three-month average turned negative (-0.05). Gold $3,623 (+2.8% vs Friday) keeps recovering from the 14-month low; Brent $91.07 (-1.6%) and WTI $82.22 as the equity sell-off drags commodities. Yields bounced with stocks — 2Y 4.76%, 10Y 5.04% (from Friday's 4.63%/4.92%). US flash PMIs due 8:45 AM CT; Williams speaks 3:00 PM CT. Wednesday's 7:30am CT cluster (core PCE, Q3 GDP 2nd estimate, claims) is the week's big data day; US markets closed Thursday for Thanksgiving. Spot levels are indicative index quotes, not executable prices.
